technical_and_design_decisions: Use Spring AMQP's BatchingRabbitTemplate to implement batching in the Rabbit sink (U1), exposing batchingEnabled and batchingSize as configurable options (default size 100).

Provide a Gradle convention/init-script based approach for module projects, leveraging the resolution of Spring Boot issue #2187 (or a workable workaround) so that Spring XD dependencies can be declared as 'provided' with a MODULE layout (U2).

Implement the DIRT runtime mode using Spring profiles / @Conditional configuration so that DB-backed components (e.g., RDBMS-backed module registry, JPA-based repositories) are conditionally loaded (U7).

Define a new core Processor<T> / MessageProcessor contract that decouples the stream-processing pipeline from any specific reactive API; the RxJava module will adapt RxJava 1.x Observable/Func1 onto that contract (U8).
Introduce a CompressionStrategy / CompressionCodec extension point with a default implementation, allowing users to override or plug in custom codecs (U4).

Reuse the existing performance benchmark harness (already used to produce prior baseline snapshots) and simply add new configuration profiles for batching and compression; results compared against previously recorded baselines (U5, U6).
Add acceptance tests for hdfs-dataset as a separate Gradle/JUnit suite wired into the CI build (U3), following existing acceptance test patterns in the codebase.
Follow existing Spring XD coding conventions, module layout, and configuration property naming to ensure consistency across all eight deliverables.

The RxJava processor module targets RxJava 1.x, which is the reactive library version contemporary with Spring XD; RxJava 2/3 are out of scope.

DIRT (Distributed In-Memory Runtime) mode is a recognized runtime concept whose behavioral boundaries are already understood; the work is about making the DB requirement optional, not defining DIRT from scratch.
Batching default size of 100 messages and batchingEnabled=true are used as the new baseline configuration per U5.
The compression extension is a follow-up to PR #1346, so the underlying compression integration already exists and this is an incremental refactor.
All eight user stories are treated as independent deliverables developed in isolation; no cross-story refactoring or shared infrastructure work is required beyond what each story implies.
